::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Aug 3 1864  
**Manuscript:** Copy outletter book British Library Add MSS. 55383 (1): P. 246
:::

Dear Miss Yonge	
[I](people/person_939.qmd) am very sorry to have missed you when you called today.

I will take my chance of finding you at [Mr Gibbs](people/person_558.qmd) tomorrow between 12 & 1 & will bring the MS which is at the printer with me.

After much searching my clerk, whom I sent to Piles Coffee House could not recover the story about the little girl[^1] I wonder if you will be able to find it

[Karamsin](other_books/otherbook_366.qmd) has been translated into French, and I saw a second hand copy in a foreign catalogue which I have ordered. There is not one in London for sale. Is it in the [London Lib](organizations/other_29.qmd).? You subscribe to it, I think.

We are going to start - in the mass, 17 souls, including bodies great and small, on Friday morning for the Isle of Wight.[^2] We mean to stay a month. Might we hope to see you there?

Yours most truly
 A. Macmillan

---

[^1]: The story of “Lotty” that CMY had seen in the *Times* and wanted to include in the *Book of Golden Deeds*.
[^2]: Macmillan, his wife and children, his sister-in-law, her children and servants.
